OKHWB · regular triangles

48 hues × 21 colored samples + 16 shared grays = 1,024 unique colors. A regular white/black lattice at every 7.5° hue angle, preserved without fitting, pruning, or fillers.

All formats ↓KritaGIMPHexVector atlas (SVG)Coordinates & measurementsCIELAB atlas / swatches →

White is the upper-left corner, black the lower-left, and the vivid hue is on the right. Each colored cell surrounds one sample in the OKHWB coordinate triangle. The shared grayscale edge appears on every page for orientation.

Point to a cell to inspect its hex value and white/black coordinates.

The shared grayscale

Sixteen evenly spaced points along W + B = 1, including black and white. Stored once in the palette.

Exact construction and measured distances

At each hue, W = i/6 and B = j/6, for nonnegative integers i + j < 6. The six rows have 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 colored samples. On the gray boundary, W = i/15 and B = 1 − i/15 for i = 0…15.

The conversion follows Ottosson’s OKHWB definition: OKHSV V = 1 − B and S = 1 − W/(1 − B), with black handled explicitly. Samples use the reference sRGB conversion and nearest-byte rounding.

Cells show nearest-sample regions in the drawn coordinate triangle. Their area does not represent perceptual distance or gamut volume. All colors remain on the requested lattice; measured distances are descriptive.
